title: Coldrif cough syrup, batch SR-13 (Sresan Pharmaceutical): toxic diethylene glycol found
reason: India's Health Ministry told Parliament that a government test found the toxic chemical diethylene glycol (DEG) at 46.28% w/v in Coldrif syrup batch SR-13, made by Sresan Pharmaceutical in Kancheepuram, Tamil Nadu. Children who died in Chhindwara, Madhya Pradesh, had taken this syrup. Tamil Nadu's State Drugs Controller cancelled the maker's manufacturing licence, and Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Odisha and Puducherry ordered the affected batches to be banned and recalled. WHO's alert N°5/2025 gives this batch's expiry date as April 2027, so packs may still be in homes. Do not use this batch. If anyone has taken it, see a doctor straight away. Because the maker's licence was cancelled, ask a pharmacist before using any Coldrif syrup.

title: Respifresh TR cough syrup, batch R01GL2523 (Rednex Pharmaceutical): toxic diethylene glycol found
reason: WHO's alert N°5/2025 lists Respifresh TR cough syrup batch R01GL2523 (made 01/2025, expiry 12/2026), made by Rednex Pharmaceutical Pvt Ltd in Ahmedabad district, Gujarat. India's drug regulator, CDSCO, reported to WHO that this batch contained diethylene glycol (DEG), a toxic chemical, at 1.34% w/v. WHO says Indian state authorities halted production at the sites involved, suspended the product authorisations and started a recall. Do not use this batch. If anyone has taken it, see a doctor straight away. If you have another batch of Respifresh TR, ask a pharmacist before using it.

reason: WHO's alert N°5/2025 lists ReLife cough syrup batch LSL25160 (made 01/2025, expiry 12/2026), made by Shape Pharma Pvt. Ltd. in Shekhpur, Gujarat. title: Everest Cumin Powder: recall of one batch ordered for pesticide residues above limits
reason: FSSAI directed Everest Food Products to recall the whole of batch E080668761 of pre-packed cumin powder. A food analyst tested a sample taken in Goa, found residues of the pesticides azoxystrobin and thiamethoxam above the prescribed limits, and declared it unsafe. The company was given a chance to appeal, and a referral food laboratory then also declared the sample unsafe. This is FSSAI's statement as reported by Business Today and Scroll. We could not open FSSAI's own notice.

title: Patanjali red chilli powder: batch recall ordered; company cites pesticide residue above limit
reason: In January 2025 FSSAI directed Patanjali Foods Limited to recall the entire batch of Red Chilli Powder (packed) with batch number AJD2400012, because it did not meet India's rules on contaminants, toxins and residues in food. The company's CEO said a tested sample did not meet the maximum permitted limit for pesticide residues. The company said it had recalled about 4 tonnes of 200 g packs and asked buyers to return the pack to where they bought it for a full refund. These are the company's statements as reported by Business Standard (PTI). One other report (ThePrint) printed the batch number as JD2400012. We found no public notice from FSSAI. If you are unsure whether your pack is affected, ask the seller or the company.

title: Hong Kong, April 2024: ethylene oxide found in samples of three MDH spice mixes and Everest Fish Curry Masala sold there
product_names: MDH Madras Curry Powder (Spice blend for Madras Curry) 100 g; MDH Sambhar Masala Mixed Masala Powder 100 g; MDH Curry Powder Mixed Masala Powder 100 g; Everest Fish Curry Masala 50 g
reason: Hong Kong's Centre for Food Safety tested samples of these four spice mixes, bought from three shops in Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong, under its routine surveillance, and found the pesticide ethylene oxide. IARC, the WHO's cancer research agency, classes ethylene oxide as a cause of cancer in humans (Group 1). The centre told the shops to stop selling the products, and the distributors and importers started recalls. The packs named had these dates: MDH Madras Curry Powder 100 g, best before end-August 2024; MDH Sambhar Masala and MDH Curry Powder Mixed Masala Powder 100 g, use by November 2024; Everest Fish Curry Masala 50 g, best before September 2025. All these dates have passed. The notice covers only these packs sold in Hong Kong and did not give the levels found. Separately, India's Health Ministry told Parliament on 26 July 2024 that FSSAI took 34 samples from MDH and Everest factories in India (25 MDH, 9 Everest) and found no ethylene oxide in them. These were not the same packs that Hong Kong tested.

title: Rajkot: FSSAI seizes about 6,500 kg of ghee from Korova Milk Product after a lab found it adulterated with vegetable fat
product_names: Ghee made by Korova Milk Product Private Limited, Rajkot
reason: FSSAI says an FSSAI-notified laboratory tested ghee samples from Korova Milk Product Private Limited, a dairy unit in Rajkot, Gujarat, and found them sub-standard and adulterated with vegetable fat. The company did not appeal. At a follow-up inspection on 20 August 2025, FSSAI seized the unit's stock of ingredients and finished goods, including about 6,500 kg of adulterated ghee worth about Rs 35 lakh. New samples were sent for testing, and further action depends on the results. This was a seizure at the factory, not a recall from shops. FSSAI did not name a brand or batch, so check the maker's name printed on your pack.

title: SDP Industries, Daman: FSSAI orders a stop to sales of all ghee the company makes
product_names: Ghee made by SDP Industries Private Limited, Daman (all variants, including Shraddha, Shree Saras and Gokul)
reason: Check the maker first: this order is only about ghee made by SDP Industries Private Limited, Daman. Other, unrelated dairies also use names such as Gokul, Saras or Shraddha, and they are not covered. According to Business Standard, on 23 August 2026 FSSAI said on X that it had ordered SDP Industries to stop selling all variants of ghee made, stored or sold from its authorised premises, with immediate effect and until further notice. FSSAI said several ghee products from this company, including variants sold under the brands Shraddha, Shree Saras and Gokul, did not meet the legal requirements across many samples and periods, so the problem could not be limited to one batch. We could not open FSSAI's own notice, and we have not checked whether the order has since been lifted. If your pack's maker is SDP Industries, Daman, ask the seller about a return or refund.
